result.title: A physics-constrained emulator for time-discretised landslide runout modelling
result.summary: Numerical simulations of landslides are commonly used to forecast impact areas. Full physics-based models provide accurate predictions, but their computational expense can preclude their use for large parameter sweeps. To achieve efficient modelling for such cases, we developed a physics-constrained neural network to emulate full landslide runout in a time-discretised manner. This emulator is trained on over 200,000 samples, each consisting of a pair of landslide thicknesses and velocities on a given DEM with a fixed time interval. To constrain the model's physical consistency, we define physics-based loss functions based on mass conservation and the system's kinetic energy loss. The model demonstrates high fidelity across the test dataset, achieving root mean square errors of approximately 0.06 m for thickness and 0.11 m/s for velocity in single-step predictions. In autoregressive rollout, these errors evolved modestly to about 0.21 m and 0.09 m/s after 110 iterations, while greatly improving computational efficiency by more than 50 times.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作训练物理约束神经网络，按固定时间间隔自回归仿真滑坡厚度与速度场演化，用质量守恒和动能损失构造损失函数，单步与 110 步 rollout 误差可控，且比全物理模型快 50 倍以上。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其多步自回归状态演进及守恒型一致性监督，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态长程更新的稳定性与长度泛化提供可核查的借鉴线索。
